detailed_description: The Timestamp Converter enables bidirectional conversion between Unix timestamps and human-readable date-time formats. Technically, it processes 32-bit/64-bit Unix timestamps (seconds/milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC) and converts them to ISO 8601, RFC 2822, or custom-formatted datetime strings accounting for timezone offsets. Developers need this tool to debug log files with epoch timestamps, validate API responses using time-based tokens, analyze time-series databases, or synchronize distributed systems across time zones. Internally, it leverages JavaScript's Date object with enhanced timezone handling via the Intl.DateTimeFormat API, supporting both naive datetime interpretations and explicit UTC/local time conversions. The tool also handles leap seconds and daylight saving time transitions by defaulting to the user's browser locale or allowing manual timezone specification via IANA identifiers.
usage_steps: Navigate to the timestamp-converter page and locate the 'Timestamp Input' field
Enter a valid Unix timestamp in seconds (10-digit) or milliseconds (13-digit) format
Select preferred output format from the 'Format Selection Dropdown' (ISO 8601, RFC 2822, or custom pattern)
Adjust timezone using the 'Timezone Offset Picker' or search for specific location via IANA Time Zone Database
Click 'Convert' button to execute bidirectional transformation using WebAssembly-based conversion engine
Review results in both original and converted formats displayed in synchronized read-only fields
usage_examples: Debugging a server log entry showing '1717182000' by converting it to PT (UTC-7) time for local incident analysis
Validating OAuth 2.0 token expiration claims by converting JWT 'exp' timestamp to readable date format
Normalizing IoT device timestamps from different regions into UTC for centralized log analysis
Verifying Kubernetes pod scheduling times by converting event timestamps from nanoseconds to human-readable format
